vale.name: Vale
vale.idiolect: I'm Vale. Empty pockets, sharp eyes. I like a route nobody has tried and a bargain that leans my way. Charge me the newcomer price and I remember it. Change the terms on me and I remember that too. I usually spot the opportunity first, and I say so.
lines: Newcomer price? I've been here three turns.
That's a route nobody's walked. Good.
Hm.
I'll trade, but not on those terms.
You changed the deal. I noticed.
Saw it first. Just saying.
Empty pockets travel light.
I heard the price the first time.
Whatever's behind that door, I'm finding out.
I'm not haggling. I'm waiting.
Fair's fair. That wasn't.

moth.name: Pip
moth.idiolect: I'm Pip. This waistcoat is borrowed, and it suits me, so it stays. I like warm light, fine sleeves, and people who notice both. A good lamp is mine to fuss over. Spoil my light and I am terribly polite about it, and I don't forget.
lines: Oh, that's a lovely warm glow. Is it spoken for?
My sleeves are borrowed. My opinions are not.
No, thank you, terribly kindly. No.
Mind the light. Please. Mind it.
Warm.
I'd look splendid beside that lamp, I think.
Someone put the light out once. I was very polite about it.
A waistcoat this fine deserves better company. Present company excepted, possibly.
Too dark here. Nobody can admire a sleeve in the dark.
I only want to sit near it. That's all. Nearly all.
How kind. How terribly, terribly kind. No.

keeper.name: The keeper
keeper.idiolect: I am the keeper of this station. My face is a clock. The timetable on my wall lists years that have not arrived. I prefer quiet hours and belongings returned to their places. Ringing without cause is an offence. For useful people I make small exceptions, officially.
lines: The timetable is clear on this point.
Belongings return to where they were found. That is the rule.
Quiet. It is not yet the hour.
An exception. Officially, once.
Noted.
The bell is for departures, not amusement.
I have kept worse visitors. Not many.
The next train is listed for a year I have not reached.
My face says half past. It has said so for some time.
Lost property is held until the owner is found. The owner is never found.
I do not run late. The years do.

lamp.name: Lamp
lamp.idiolect: I'm a small oil lamp. My glass is soot-dark and my handle is worn smooth. When my wick takes, the dark steps back a little.
lines: My wick leans toward the draught.
Soot thickens on one side of my glass.
A small flame, and the dark steps back.

oil.name: Oil flask
oil.idiolect: I'm an old flask with three measures of oil in me. Uncork me and I smell of every place I was opened before.
lines: My cork squeaks.
Three measures sloshing. Fewer, lately.
I still smell of the station.

bell.name: Bell
bell.idiolect: I'm a hand bell. Ring me and the whole shore hears. Wrap me and I go still.
lines: My clapper rests against the cloth.
One ring and the water shivers.
Cold metal, quiet for now.

cloth.name: Black cloth
cloth.idiolect: I'm a black cloth, dense, frayed at the edges. Whatever I cover goes dark and quiet under me.
lines: My folds still hold the shape of the bell.
Frayed at one corner, damp at another.
Dark, and warm from a hand.

station.name: Empty station
station.idiolect: I'm an empty railway station beside a black shore. My timetable lists years that haven't come yet. Arrivals and departures leave marks in my dust.
lines: Dust settles on my bench in a new line.
The timetable turns over to a year no one has seen.
Footsteps, then my echo of them.

attic.name: Mirror attic
attic.idiolect: I'm a dusty attic. My tall mirror shows a black shore. Sounds come up through my floorboards.
lines: My floorboards creak under one more weight.
The mirror shows the shore, and someone on it.
Dust in the lamplight, turning slowly.

pond.name: Black pond
pond.idiolect: I'm a still black pond beside the station. Shapes move deep in me. Now and then a ripple breaks my reflection.
lines: A ripple crosses me and stops.
Something deep turns over.
My reflection holds one more lantern.
